aspect: EXAMPLE - the rate and the streak
description: BLS recorded a fatal injury rate of 4.3 per 100,000 FTE for Hispanic or Latino workers in 2024, down from 4.4 in 2023 - the eighth consecutive year with the highest death rate of any group, against an all-worker rate of 3.3.
energy_note: Eight years running, the most likely to die at work.

aspect: EXAMPLE - and most of them are immigrants
description: Of the 1,229 fatalities among Hispanic or Latino workers in 2024, 68.5% - 842 - were foreign-born.
energy_note: Eight hundred and forty-two men who had come to work.

aspect: EXAMPLE - construction, and a rising share
description: In 2021, 274 fatalities among foreign-born Hispanic or Latino workers accounted for 27% of all deaths in the construction industry, up from 19.8% in 2011. Falls, slips and trips were the most common fatal event.
energy_note: A quarter of everyone who dies on a site.

aspect: THE HONEST GAP - no rate exists for the intersection
description: BLS does not publish fatality rates by race or ethnicity for specific industries or occupations - only counts. So there is no published fatality rate for Hispanic construction workers specifically, and anyone quoting one has made it up.
energy_note: The number everyone wants does not exist.

aspect: Reporting the hazard is what ends the job
description: The man who raises the missing harness is the man not called for the next job, so the safety system depends on complaints from precisely the people who cannot afford to make them.
energy_note: Safety depends on a complaint he cannot afford.
